title: Flag numeric performance targets that lack a baseline and estimate
summary: Add a convention, in the reader and planner prompts and in code, that a numeric performance target (such as wall time under N minutes) must cite a measured base-commit baseline and a per-component estimate within the change scope. A reading that carries such a target without both is marked unproven and flagged to the user in its question before dispatch. A unit test shows that an unbacked target is flagged. The audience is the user who approves readings, and the reader, planner and verifier agents who follow the convention.

defaults_applied.how: New unit tests for flagged and not-flagged readings; cargo test and clippy must pass.
The rule is enforced by a code check on readings. The parts that cannot be checked by code (the planner and doc wording) are marked prose-only.
Criteria require the test to show an unbacked target being flagged, and a backed one not being flagged.
No new crate is needed; simple string scanning is enough.
One focused change in the reading path, plus prompt and doc text.
The check and tests are in Rust.
The verifier runs cargo test, clippy and fmt --check.
Docs and code comments are written for an outside reader.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The mechanism is a post-processing step in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs, beside ensure_changelog. It scans acceptance criteria for a numeric performance target: a number with a time unit, or a latency or throughput word, next to words like under, within, below or at most.

A target counts as backed only if the reading text cites a baseline (the word 'baseline' plus a measured figure or source) and a per-component estimate. Otherwise the step sets the reading's question field to an 'unproven target' flag and adds an assumption saying the target is unproven. Athena's existing flow that surfaces the question to the user before dispatch is the flagging path.
The step uses plain string and character scanning, with no new crate, to stay small. It is a heuristic, and the convention doc says so.

The convention text goes into the reader and planner prompts under crates/athena-context/prompts/, and into docs/design/job-planning.md or docs/enforcement.md. It states that the code check is a heuristic and the rest is prose-only. defaults.toml, athena.toml and the workflows are untouched, because a new standing default would change owner-governed files.
Prompt edits may require bumping prompt versions or fixing prompt-budget and pin tests. The producer should run cargo test to find out.
CHANGELOG.md is already auto-added to change readings.

acceptance_criteria.text: The reader and planner prompts state the convention: a numeric performance target must cite a measured baseline from the base commit and a per-component estimate showing it is reachable within the allowed change scope. Without both, the target is called unproven and is flagged to the user before dispatch.
The convention is written down in a design or enforcement doc under docs/. The doc says which part is enforced by code (the flag on unbacked numeric targets) and which part is prose-only.

A new unit test in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs builds a reading whose criterion says 'wall time under 10 minutes' with no baseline or estimate. After the new check runs, the reading's question contains an 'unproven' flag and an assumption records it. Run `cargo test -p athena-core reading` and see it pass.

A companion test shows that a reading whose numeric target cites a baseline and a per-component estimate is not flagged. A reading with no numeric performance target (for example 'tests pass') is also not flagged. Run `cargo test -p athena-core reading` and see both pass.

The check runs inside the reading-construction path, next to ensure_changelog, so a real reading is flagged without extra calls. `cargo test` passes workspace-wide, including prompt budget and pin tests, `cargo clippy --all-targets` is clean, and `cargo fmt --check` passes.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry for the convention. No file outside the listed deliverables changes, and athena.toml, defaults.toml and .github/workflows are untouched.

out_of_scope: Measuring baselines automatically or running benchmarks.
Changing athena.toml, defaults.toml or the CI workflows.
Natural-language-complete detection of every performance phrasing; the check is a heuristic.
departures: Slightly higher cost and time than the reference: the change spans code, prompts and docs, and prompt edits may trip pin or budget tests.
hard_reason: Touches the gate that judges readings before dispatch, so a wrong heuristic can silently pass or wrongly flag jobs.
